question: The total surface area of a cuboid is 4200 cm². If the length and breadth of the cuboid are 15 cm and 16 cm, then find the height of the cuboid.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for height when TSA, length (l), and breadth (b) are given:

Height = (TSA ÷ 2 − l × b) ÷ (l + b)

Height = (4200 ÷ 2 − 15 × 16) ÷ (15 + 16)

Height = (2100 − 240) ÷ 31 = 1860 ÷ 31 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f0c82f5bf514b53c9e89252b5c795a92054d29f4be3e07a2303f5fcc6c3f235.png] 

**Given:**

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 4200 cm²

Length (l) = 15 cm

Breadth (b) = 16 cm

**Formula Used:**

TSA of a cuboid = 2(l × b + b × h + h × l)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4200 = 2(15 × 16 + 16 × h + h × 15)

⇒ 2100 = 240 + 16h + 15h

⇒ 2100 = 240 + 31h

⇒ 31h = 2100 − 240

⇒ 31h = 1860

⇒ h = 1860 ÷ 31 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The space occupied by the cuboid is calculated as: Volume = l × b × h

Lateral Surface Area

The area of the four side walls excluding top and bottom: LSA = 2h(l + b)

Length of Diagonal

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid: Diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²)
